sentences: The largest driver of default risk is revolving credit utilization, the share of the credit limit an applicant is using, and risk rises steeply with it.
Risk climbs most sharply once utilization passes about 0.735, where the contribution to default risk is highest.
Past delinquencies are the next most important factor, and any delinquency raises risk compared with none.
Higher income is associated with lower default risk, though its effect is smaller than that of utilization or delinquencies.
Utilization and credit history length are included in the model as an interaction, but the data do not settle whether the effect of utilization depends on history length.
Credit history length has at most a weak effect on predicted risk, and its direction is not firmly established.
Debt-to-income ratio hardly matters, since no movement in its effect is resolved at this sample size.
The remaining features, including age, the two application attributes and recent credit inquiries, have effects that are negligible.
